**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Religious Studies 3 (0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Paper 3: The New Testament, Religion in Relation to Philosophy, Ethics and Morality, Historical Development of Islam (570CE-661CE). Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

The paper has six sections of six questions each: Section 2.1 The Gospel According to Luke (questions 1-6); Section 2.2 The Fourth Gospel (questions 7-12); Section 2.3 The Early Church as Reflected in Acts and 1 Corinthians (questions 13-18); Section 4.1 Philosophy of Religion (questions 19-24); Section 4.2 Ethics and Morality (questions 25-30); Section 6.0 The Historical Development of Islam (570CE - 661CE) (questions 31-36).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Points : chaque question porte 25 marks imprimés (« All questions carry equal marks »). Aucun écart constaté : les questions à plusieurs parties somment bien 25 (Q4 : 9 + 8 + 8 ; Q31 : 12 + 13 ; Q36 : 5 + 20). Les points imprimés n'ont pas été modifiés.

Sujet scanné de trois pages (page de garde puis 36 questions en six sections de six) : filigrane gcerevision.com et texte fantôme du verso ignorés ; aucune question illisible, aucune figure ni carte. Les doubles espaces imprimés ont été normalisés.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level, avec des références bibliques ou islamiques limitées à celles que l'auteur tient pour sûres ; formulations prudentes (« according to Islamic tradition », « Christians believe »). À faire relire par un spécialiste (théologie chrétienne, histoire de l'islam, philosophie de la religion) avant mise en avant.

Question 3 : l'orthographe imprimée « Caeserea Philippi » est conservée dans l'énoncé. Luc 9:18-20 ne nomme pas le lieu (Marc 8 et Matthieu 16 le nomment) ; le corrigé le dit, et signale que les traditions chrétiennes comprennent différemment « le rocher » de Matthieu 16.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Discuss the implications of Peter's profession of faith at Caeserea Philippi.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Peter's profession of faith is one of the turning points of the Gospels. In Mark 8:27-30 and Matthew 16:13-20 the scene is set in the region of Caesarea Philippi, and Luke records the same confession (Luke 9:18-20) without naming the place. In answer to the question "Who do you say that I am?", Peter replies that Jesus is the Christ, "the Christ of God" in Luke. This answer has several implications for the identity of Jesus, for the disciples and for the church.

**1. The identity of Jesus.** Peter speaks for the Twelve and for the first time names Jesus as the Messiah, the anointed one promised in the Old Testament. The crowds had thought of Jesus as John the Baptist, Elijah or one of the prophets (Luke 9:19). Peter's answer shows that the disciples had gone further than public opinion.

**2. A redefinition of Messiahship.** Jesus at once forbids the disciples to tell anyone (Luke 9:21) and speaks of the Son of Man who must suffer, be rejected, be killed and be raised on the third day (Luke 9:22). Many Jews expected a political and military Messiah. Jesus teaches that his Messiahship passes through suffering. Peter's confession is therefore correct in its words but must be corrected in its meaning, as Mark 8:32-33 shows when Peter rebukes Jesus and is rebuked in turn.

**3. The cost of discipleship.** Luke follows the prediction with the call to deny oneself, take up the cross daily and follow Jesus (Luke 9:23-25). To confess Jesus as the Christ means to share his path.

**4. The place of Peter.** In Matthew's version Jesus calls Peter blessed and speaks of building his church on this rock and of the keys of the kingdom (Matthew 16:17-19). Christian traditions understand these words in different ways: some see Peter himself as the foundation, others see his faith or the confession as the foundation. All agree that Peter holds a leading place among the apostles. Luke does not record these words, but he shows Peter's later role when Jesus tells him to strengthen his brothers (Luke 22:31-32) and in the leadership of Peter in Acts.

**5. A link with the Transfiguration and the journey to Jerusalem.** Luke places the Transfiguration eight days after the confession (Luke 9:28-36), where the voice from heaven confirms that Jesus is the Son and the Chosen One, and then turns toward Jerusalem (Luke 9:51). The confession prepares the disciples for the Passion.

**6. Limits.** Peter's faith is real but incomplete: he later denies Jesus (Luke 22:54-62). The confession is the beginning, not the end, of understanding.

**Conclusion.** The profession of faith implies that Jesus is the Messiah, that Messiahship means suffering service, that discipleship means following the same road, and that Peter has a leading role in the community of the disciples. It is the hinge on which the story of the Gospel turns toward Jerusalem.
